answers.stem_only: Status page: it tolerates stale data, so switch its GetItem calls to eventually consistent reads, which cost half the read capacity of strongly consistent reads. Report job: a Scan consumes read capacity for every item it reads, and a filter expression does not reduce that; give open orders a sparse attribute with a sparse global secondary index and Query that index, so the job reads only the few open orders and does not touch the base table's read capacity.

This is a hot key: all writes go to one item, so one partition receives far more writes than its per-partition write limit, even though table-level capacity is unused. Raising table capacity or switching to on-demand does not lift the per-partition limit. Use write sharding: spread each contest's counter over several items with a calculated or random suffix on the key, and sum the shards when reading the total.

Recordings of several MB exceed the DynamoDB item size limit and are rarely read; store them as objects in Amazon S3 (with a low-cost storage class or lifecycle if desired) and keep the S3 object key in the DynamoDB item as a pointer.

Use optimistic locking: add a version number attribute, increment it on every save, and make the PutItem conditional (condition expression) on the version that was read. A failed condition (ConditionalCheckFailedException) tells the application to reload. A plain conditional write is cheaper than a transaction, which consumes twice the write capacity.
